questions.question: People who wear bifocal lenses have _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**presbyopia.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The gradual loss of your eyes' capacity to focus on** adjacent things **is known as presbyopia.
 
• It commonly appears in your **early to mid-40s** and worsens until you reach the **age of 65.**
 
• Presbyopia is caused by the** ciliary muscles weakening** and the eye lens becoming less flexible with age. As a result, the **eye's accommodation power** is lost, and the user is unable to view nearer objects well.
 
• **Glasses with bifocal power** and appropriate **focal lengths** are frequently used to remedy this problem. The **upper half** of the lens is** concave,** which corrects **myopia** and allows you to **see distant objects **clearly, while the** lower part** is** convex,** which corrects** hypermetropia** and allows you to see **nearer items** clearly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypermetropia**__** **

 __
 
• A person with **hypermetropia/hyperopia,** also known as **long sight,** can** see objects clearly from afar** but not up close.
 
• When the** eye is shorter than normal** or the** cornea is overly flat**, light rays **focus behind the retina**, causing hypermetropia (long-sightedness). The retina cannot concentrate light rays from close objects, such as book pages, clearly.
 
• It is **corrected **by spectacles or contact lenses with lenses that are** 'plus' or convex in shape.**
 
 
 
• **​Myopia__**
 __
 
• ​**Nearsightedness (myopia)** is a vision problem in which** items close** to you are **clearly seen** but objects further away are **blurry.**
 
• When light rays bend (refract) wrongly due to the structure of your eye,** focusing images in front of your retina** instead of on your retina.
 
• When one spends too much time in a **state of near focus**, myopia worsens. Activities like **reading **for extended periods of time or **knitting** might aggravate the issue.
 
• Myopia glasses commonly have a** concave (inwardly curved) lens**, which shifts the light's focus to help you see well. Myopia is corrected by **single vision lenses.**
 
 
 
• **​Cataract__**
 
 
• ​Cataract occurs when the normal lens of your eye becomes** hazy. Proteins** in your lens degrade, making objects appear **fuzzy, foggy, or less colourful.**
 
• The** most common** cause is** ageing.** This is due to the regular ageing of the eyes, which begins around the **age of 40.**
 
• **Other causes** of cataracts include someone having** cataracts in your family members**, having certain **medical problems** like diabetes, smoking, having had an **eye injury**,** eye surgery,** or** radiation treatments** on your upper body, having spent a lot of time in the** sun**, especially without sunglasses that protect your eyes from** damaging ultraviolet (UV) rays**, or using certain medications, such as** corticosteroids, **which may cause the early formation of cataracts.
 
• **Cataract surgery** is the only **effective treatment** for cataracts.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important for individual health?

• **Public transport is NOT important for individual health.**
 
• Individual hygiene:
 
• Good hygiene is important for cleanliness.
 
• Good hygiene prevents illness.
 
• Good hygiene practices are:
 
 
• Brushing teeth daily.
 
• Bathing daily.
 
• Washing hair regularly.
 
• Wearing clean and tidy clothes daily.

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **a part of the hind-brain?
questions.solution:
__**Hypothalamus**__ is NOT correct.

__
 
• **Hindbrain Parts: These parts are Pons, Medulla Oblongata, and the Cerebellum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Functions of hindbrain**

 
 
• It is responsible for controlling the lungs as well as the heart. It also controls **heart rate, breathing, blood pressure, sneezing, and swallowing**.
 
• The cerebellum helps in coordinating the various muscles that enable the voluntary movements we make.
 
• The cranial nerves in the medulla oblongata also have many functions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Human brain:**

 
 
• On average, an adult brain weighs between 1.0 kg - 1.5 kg. It is mainly composed of neurons – the fundamental unit of the brain and nervous system. 
 
• **Parts of Human Brain:**
 
 
• **Forebrain **– Largest part of the brain
 
 
• It is the anterior part of the brain. The forebrain parts include:
 
• Cerebrum
 
• **Hypothalamus**__
 
• Thalamus
 
• Forebrain Function: Controls the reproductive functions, body temperature, emotions, hunger, and sleep.
 
 
 
• **Midbrain**: Smallest and central part of the brain
 
 
• The midbrain consists of:
 
• Tectum
 
• Tegmentum
 
 
 
• **Hindbrain**: The lower part of the brain
 
 
• Cerebellum
 
• Medulla
 
• Pons

questions.question: Which virus is responsible for causing common cold?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rhinovirus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Rhinovirus** is the most common cause of the **common cold**.
 
• It belongs to the family of **Picornaviridae**, which are small RNA viruses.

questions.question: Which part of the digestive system receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Small Intestines.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Small Intestine of the digestive system receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas.
 
• **The Small Intestine:**
 
 
• It is highly coiled and is about 6-8 meters long. It receives secretions from the liver and the pancreas.
 
• The digested food can now pass into the blood vessels in the wall of the intestine. This process is called **absorption**.
 
• The inner walls of the small intestine have thousands of finger-like outgrowths.
 
• These are called **villi.** (It increases the surface area of absorption of the digested food).
 
• The small intestine receives bile juice and stores it in the gall bladder.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Large intestine:**

 
 
• It is wider and shorter than the small intestine.
 
• It is about 1.5 meters in length.
 
• Its function is to absorb water and some salts from the undigested food material.
 
 
 
• **Gallbladder:**
 
 
• The gallbladder is a pear-shaped organ under the liver.
 
• It stores bile, a fluid made by the liver to digest fat.
 
• It breaks down fats into fatty acids, which can be taken into the body by the digestive tract.
 
 
 
• **The stomach:**
 
 
• It is a muscular hollow organ.
 
• It takes in food from the oesophagus (gullet or food pipe), mixes it, breaks it down, and then passes it on to the small intestine in small portions.
 
• The stomach stores the food for 4-5 hours.
 
• The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the chyme.
 
• Gastric juice is made up of digestive enzymes, hydrochloric acid, and other substances that are important for absorbing nutrients - about 3 to 4 litres of gastric juice are produced per day.
 
• The hydrochloric acid in the gastric juice breaks down the food and the digestive enzymes split up the proteins.
 
• The acidic gastric juice also kills bacteria.

questions.question: A child is a picky eater. He does not consume milk at all and barely eats other kinds of food. When he started losing his baby teeth, they were not getting replaced with new teeth. This can be solved by giving him _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium supplements**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium is an essential **mineral** required for the development and maintenance of **strong bones and teeth**.
 
• In children, a lack of calcium can lead to **poor dental health**, including delayed eruption of new teeth.
 
• Calcium plays a crucial role in the process of **tooth formation** (odontogenesis) by strengthening the teeth's enamel and dentin.
 
• Milk and dairy products are primary sources of calcium, but for a child who is a **picky eater** and avoids milk, **calcium supplements** can serve as an alternative.
 
• Calcium deficiency in children can also lead to **weakened bones**, increasing the risk of conditions such as rickets.
 
• Providing calcium supplements, along with a balanced diet, ensures that the child gets the recommended daily intake of calcium for healthy growth.
 
• Other dietary sources of calcium include **leafy green vegetables, fortified cereals, tofu, and nuts.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vitamin B Complex**__

 __
 
• **Vitamin B complex** includes a group of water-soluble vitamins that play a role in **metabolism, energy production, and red blood cell formation.**
 
• A deficiency of vitamin B may lead to **fatigue, anemia, or nerve issues**, but it is not directly linked to tooth development.
 
 
 
• **Carbohydrate-rich Food**__
 __
 
• **Carbohydrates** are the primary source of **energy** for the body.
 
• While they are important for overall health, they do not contribute to **tooth development** or the replacement of teeth.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin C**__
 
 
• **Vitamin C** is vital for the **repair and growth of tissues** and supports the immune system.
 
• A deficiency of vitamin C can lead to conditions like **scurvy**, but it does not directly impact tooth formation or calcium absorption.

questions.question: What is Agraphia?

options.text: Loss of the ability to understand
Loss of the ability to speak
Loss of the ability to hear
Loss of the ability to write

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Loss of ability to write.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agraphia is an acquired neurological disorder causing a loss in the ability to communicate through writing**, either due to some form of motor dysfunction or an inability to spell.
 
• Agraphia can be broadly divided into central and peripheral categories. Central agraphia typically involves language areas of the brain, causing difficulty spelling or with spontaneous communication, and is often accompanied by other language disorders.
 
• **Peripheral agraphia** usually targets motor and visuospatial skills in addition to language and tends to involve motoric areas of the brain, causing difficulty in the movements associated with writing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hearing impairment: **

 
 
• A person having difficulty in hearing is said to have a hearing impairment.
 
• "Deaf” means persons having 70 DB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears.
 
• "Hard of hearing” means a person having 60 DB to 70 DB hearing loss in speech frequencies in both ears.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a protozoa parasite of Leishmania species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Kala Azar.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Kala Azar **disease is caused by a protozoa parasite of the Leishmania species.
 
• Leishmania donovani is a parasitic protozoan belonging to the class Mastigophora or flagellata.
 
 
• It is a human parasite that is dimorphic (i.e. shows two forms) & digenetic in nature
 
• It causes the disease Kala-azar or Dumdum fever by sand fly (phelobotomus). 
 
• Cutaneous Leishmaniasis - Skin ulcers.
 
• Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis - Ulcers in mouth, throat, and nose, Nosebleed, Difficulty in breathing.
 
• Visceral Leishmaniasis - Weakness, weight loss, loss of appetite, enlarged spleen, liver, lymph nodes, and a decrease in the production of blood cells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
